title: Treasury liquidity-support buyback operation (2-3Y nominal, 1:40pm ET)
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Buyback Operations (August 2026 refunding quarter), masthead "For Publication September 9, 2026" — the REPLACEMENT schedule press release sb0607 (2026-08-19) promised, re-fetched direct 2026-09-15 (plain curl, HTTP 200, 89,250 bytes, md5 c49a5351bf2d31a367817abc62be51bd) and its PDF text layer independently decompressed. This SUPERSEDES the 125,547-byte / md5 79b65955e74a59f6bebff3adf8ba7b35 August-5 document every prior fetch on this entry read. This row is byte-for-byte unchanged across the two: announce 10/5/2026, operation 10/6/2026 1:40 pm - 2:00 pm, settle 10/7/2026, Liquidity Support, Nominal Coupons 2Y to 3Y, maturity range 10/07/2028 - 10/06/2029, min $0, max $4 billion. Stays estimate on the same two counts: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and the confirming primary is the 10-05 operation announcement rather than this document. Re-verified at the primary 2026-09-15
notes: It shares its date AND its tenor with treasury-3y-note-2026-10-06, running 1:40-2:00pm ET — forty minutes after that auction's 1:00pm competitive close. That combination corrects a claim the September sibling ledger (treasury-3y-note-2026-09-08) carried in every row: 'the buyback lever does not reach this tenor.' True for September, false for this date. Two details. The $4B cap is the STANDING liquidity-support cap for short nominal buckets, NOT the figure press release sb0607 (2026-08-19) doubled — that raised the 10-20Y and 20-30Y caps which this same schedule still shows at $2B, so unlike treasury-buyback-10y20y-2026-10-15 this row's cap is current rather than superseded. And the maturity range 10/07/2028 - 10/06/2029 INCLUDES the September 3-Year's 2029-09-15 maturity while EXCLUDING the 10-06 issue's own 2029-10-15, so the operation can bid for the note this auction displaces but never for the auction's own security; Treasury's footnotes put the preliminary eligible-CUSIP list at 11:00am ET on 10-05 and the final list at 11:00am ET on 10-06, i.e. two hours before bidders commit. READ IT, DO NOT TRADE IT, and specifically do not read it as auction support: measured 2026-09-05 from fiscaldata's buybacks_operations dataset, buyback operations landed on a 3-Year auction date 10 times in the 29-auction constant-$58B era, and fill rates track the BUCKET rather than the auction day (10Y-20Y fills its cap 25/25 regardless; the 2Y-3Y bucket runs a 60% mean fill over 9 ops, and of the two variance-carrying buckets that ever shared a 3Y auction day, 2Y-3Y filled 100% on 2025-03-11 while 7Y-10Y filled 11% against a 10% mean on 2024-09-10 — one observation each way, no significance test applied). That n=1-each-way split is registered as FT-treasury-3y-note-2026-10-06-2. Discovered during the treasury-3y-note-2026-10-06 initial research (2026-09-05); the same schedule's 10-02 (10-20Y) and 10-08 (20-30Y) operations were seen and deliberately not filed here — the 10-08 one lands on the 30-Year bond auction's own day and belongs to that event's sweep. AMENDED 2026-09-05 by this event's own initial research (docs/research/events/treasury-buyback-2y3y-2026-10-06.md); status, date, cap and impact UNCHANGED, two claims above CORRECTED. (1) 'the operation can bid for the note this auction displaces' is wrong in outcome though right about the range: reconstructed from the nine BBA_*.xml final announcements diffed against buybacks_security_details, no security has ever been eligible before its first coupon paid — zero false positives across 9 of 9 operations — so the September 3-Year 91282CRL7 (matures 2029-09-15, first coupon 2027-03-15) CANNOT be bought, nor can any of the six 3-Year notes issued 2026-04-15 through 2026-09-15; 91282CQJ3 misses by nine days. The newest note this operation can touch is the March 2026 3-Year, and the expected eligible count is 32-34. (2) The '60% mean fill over 9 ops' figure is right but understates the contrast: at the $4B cap (n=8) the full-cap fill is 1 of 8, mean accepted $2.181B, median $2.281B, range $0.358-4.000B, and only 2025-03-11 ever cleared $2.79B. The programme is BARBELLED — full-cap fills run 1Mo-2Y 10/10, 2Y-3Y 2/9, 3Y-5Y 4/10, 5Y-7Y 0/10, 7Y-10Y 0/9, 10Y-20Y 25/25, 20Y-30Y 24/26 — so the long-end ledgers' 'the cap binds, not demand' model does not describe this bucket at all. Two further findings. The 10-20Y sibling's offer-collapse story does NOT read across: 2Y-3Y offers ran $4.75-12.46B and the ALL-TIME HIGH is the most recent operation (2026-07-09), with cover never above 3.12x here versus 3.7-18x at the long end. And the single same-day-auction precedent is confounded — 2025-03-11 is both the only full fill and the sample's VIX peak at 26.92, though the Spearman rank correlation of VIX to fill across all nine is -0.083, so neither stress nor the auction predicts it. 10-06 is also the ONLY 2Y-3Y operation in the entire 17-operation August-refunding schedule. Registered as FT-treasury-buyback-2y3y-2026-10-06-1 (the eligible list) and -2 (accepted below $2.79B, the deliberate complement of FT-treasury-3y-note-2026-10-06-2). AMENDED 2026-09-15 (D-21 pulse, docs/research/events/treasury-buyback-2y3y-2026-10-06.md); date, cap, tenor, maturity range and impact UNCHANGED, source re-pointed to the 09-09 replacement schedule, and this entry's CENTRAL MECHANISM SUPERSEDED. (1) The replacement schedule sb0607 promised was PUBLISHED 2026-09-09 and made SIX long-end rows read "= or > $4 billion" (09-24, 10-01, 10-08, 10-15, 10-27, 11-04) while leaving THIS row a flat $4 billion, 7Y-10Y (09-17) and 1Mo-2Y (11-05) likewise $4B, and TIPS $500M/$750M; the quarter now runs 20 operations (10Y-20Y five, 20Y-30Y four) against the 17 recorded above, and 2Y-3Y is STILL exactly one. So the "cap is current, not superseded" note above is retired on its own terms: the $2B long-end figure it compared against no longer exists. (2) The BARBELL finding recorded above is superseded as a mechanism. The 2026-09-10 10Y-20Y operation ran at a $6B cap, offered $10.489B (cover 1.75x) and accepted $5.187B = 86.5% across 23 of 40 eligible issues — the 10Y-20Y bucket's first non-full fill in 26 operations, and it bought 23 issues where every prior 2026 operation in that bucket bought 1-5. Recomputed over all 99 nominal Liquidity Support operations at caps above $100M: cover >= 2.5x fills its cap 63/72 (88%), cover < 2.5x fills 1/19 (5%), Spearman fill-to-cover +0.719; at caps of $4B or more (n=43) the lowest cover at which a full fill has ever occurred is 2.56x and 0 of 30 below that line have filled. The long end was never special — its $2B cap simply sat far below a $7.4-36.0B offer book. Figures computed only over cover >= 1.2x, since fill <= cover arithmetically. (3) This EXPLAINS AWAY 2025-03-11, the single full fill the same-day-3-Year-auction story rests on: it printed 2.67x cover, above the line and predicted by the rule, leaving nothing for the shared auction date or the VIX 26.92 print to explain — which removes the sole supporting observation under FT-treasury-3y-note-2026-10-06-2. (4) FT-treasury-buyback-2y3y-2026-10-06-2 (accepted < $2.79B) STANDS and now rests on a mechanism: this bucket's cover has run 1.19-3.12x, median 2.15x, above 2.56x in 2 of 8 at this cap. Counter-caveat: 09-10's 86.5% is the highest fill ever recorded below 2.5x cover. FT-treasury-buyback-2y3y-2026-10-06-3 registered on the cover rule itself (scores 2026-10-07). Environment: CPI 09-11 core +0.3%/2.4% above consensus, FOMC 09-16 priced 87.5% to HIKE 25bp (Polymarket, $175.8M book, fetched 09-15), 2Y/3Y +28bp since 09-04 to 4.65/4.73, VIX 14.53 -> 17.68. STILL read-it-do-not-trade-it; `symbols: []`, no house playbook is rates-keyed.
